C0.quote: Several voting procedures, as well as other collective decision-making mechanisms
C0.note: Collective decision mechanisms (RR, MNW, leximin) for sequences of decisions; framed as public decision-making / perpetual voting, with Borda-based ordinal inputs.

C1.quote: We thus introduce a new fairness property that captures this requirement
C1.note: Main results are which mechanisms satisfy which fairness properties, plus impossibility results. Computational intractability is only remarked on briefly.

C2.1.value: valuations (agents' valuations; ordinal preference orders translated by Borda)
C2.1.quote: every agent i reports her valuation

C2.2.quote: we translate the ordinal preference orders to cardinal preferences
C2.2.note: General model uses cardinal valuations. Borda valuations come from reported strict rankings.

C2.3.quote: each agent evaluates the candidates in each round
C2.3.note: Refers to agents' preferences, utilities and evaluations.

C2.4.quote: We assume that the agents have additive utility functions.
C2.4.note: Valuations are described as reported but also used as the agents' utilities. The mechanisms are applied directly, with no statement relating reports to held attitudes.

C3.2.note: No statement that voters submit their held attitude.

C4.1.quote: we translate the ordinal preference orders to cardinal preferences
C4.1.note: Rankings are mapped to Borda valuations, which are used as utilities.

C4.2.quote: they assign either 1 or 0 to each candidate
C4.2.note: Dichotomous valuations are defined as values 1 or 0. This appears only in the appendix, on a side axiom.

C5.1.quote: each one of the agents will get at least a 1/n fraction
C5.1.note: Proportionality, Pareto optimality and leximin are evaluated in the results.

C5.2.note: Evaluated on the reported valuations. No statement relates them to held attitudes.

VOT.quote_behav: every agent i reports her valuation
VOT.note: Agents' valuations are exogenous inputs. In offline RR the agent's choice is a rule of the mechanism.

C8.1.note: NA: no STRAT or MIXED type.

claims.quote: a decision-making mechanism must consider fairness notions
the leximin mechanism guarantees the best possible additive approximation to proportionality
has a significant advantage over the other known mechanisms

C9.1.note: Claims about fairness to agents and which mechanism is preferable.

C9.2.note: Fairness claims for agents need reported valuations to equal true valuations, and this is not stated. Mapping from ordinal to cardinal is stated via Borda.
